idiom_name: arr.length = n / slice copy + readonly T[] views (typed arrays: slice, not subarray)
implementation_notes: The runtime is JavaScript, so the mechanics are the JavaScript ones - setting length truncates ('elements beyond the new length are deleted'), a slice copies into a new array, and for binary data slice() copies while subarray() shares the parent ArrayBuffer. TypeScript's contribution is expressing the decision so it cannot be undone by accident: ReadonlyArray<T>/readonly T[] marks the trimmed value as one nobody writes to ('mainly a tool we can use for intent'), and a user-defined type predicate turns the filtering phase into a narrowing so the surviving elements carry the type the rest of the code sees. Neither changes the allocation - ReadonlyArray 'has no representation at runtime' - so the buffer is still the engine's business and readonly is documentation plus compile-time enforcement, not a smaller array.
code_sketch:
const kept = rows.filter((r): r is LiveRow => r.state === "live");  // narrowed copy
rows = kept;                                  // the old peak-sized array is dropped
const frozen: readonly LiveRow[] = kept;      // further growth is a compile error
// binary data: new Uint8Array(buf.slice(0, n)) copies; subarray() shares
pitfalls: readonly/ReadonlyArray is erased at runtime ('no representation at runtime'): a cast, a plain-JS consumer or Object.assign can still write through it.

A type predicate is trusted, not verified: a wrong guard makes the narrowed element type a lie, and narrowing applies only where the type is recomputed - a variable typed before the filter keeps the old wide type.
A Uint8Array view has a small static type but keeps the whole parent buffer alive; the type system says nothing about the allocation behind a view, so the buffer must be copied explicitly.
sources: MDN, Array: length - setting length smaller than the current length truncates the array and deletes the elements beyond it: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array/length

typescriptlang.org, Object Types - 'The ReadonlyArray Type': 'a special type that describes arrays that shouldn't be changed', the readonly T[] shorthand, 'Unlike Array, there isn't a ReadonlyArray constructor', and the tuple note that it 'has no representation at runtime': https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/objects.html
